activity_context.topic_title: Finding a Basis of the Null Space of a Matrix

feedback.problem: Find a basis of the null space of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find a basis of $\text{Null}(A),$ we need to solve the equation $Ax=0$ and express the solution as a linear combination of linearly independent vectors. Those vectors form a basis of $\text{Null}(A).$

The given matrix is already in reduced row echelon form. So, the equation $Ax=0$ corresponds to the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{4}=0 \\ {x}_{2}+2{x}_{4}=0 \\ {x}_{3}-3{x}_{4}=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}={x}_{4} \\ {x}_{2}=-2{x}_{4} \\ {x}_{3}=3{x}_{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Here, ${x}_{1}$, ${x}_{2}$, and ${x}_{3}$ are basic variables corresponding to the pivot columns ($1$st, $2$nd, and $3$rd) and ${x}_{4}$ is a free variable corresponding to the non-pivot column. Therefore, if $x\in \text{Null}(A),$ then

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3} \\ {x}_{4}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{4} \\ -2{x}_{4} \\ 3{x}_{4} \\ {x}_{4}\end{aligned}]={x}_{4}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],
$$

where ${x}_{4}\in R.$ This implies that

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}
$$

is a basis of $\text{Null}(A)$ since it is a linearly independent set and its vectors generate the $\text{Null}(A).$
